S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is characterized by a chronically low mood lasting at least two years in adults, with only brief periods of remission. Individuals often function day to day but at a reduced level, experiencing the depression as part of their usual personality or life, which can delay recognition and treatment. Compared with major depressive disorder, the symptoms are typically less acute but more enduring, leading to long-term interpersonal, occupational, and quality-of-life impairment. It frequently coexists with other psychiatric conditions and may be punctuated by superimposed major depressive episodes ("double depression").

patient.stressor: Brad’s low-grade depression emerged insidiously in the years following his retirement from biomedical engineering, a transition he had initially approached with excitement about having more time for art, music, and mentoring. After the first year of novelty—setting up his studio, joining the chess club, and volunteering with robotics teams—he began to feel a subtle but persistent sense that his projects "didn’t really matter" now that he was no longer contributing to a large R&D group. Over the next three years, he continued to attend community events and hiking club outings, but his wife noticed he talked more about his peak career achievements than about current plans, and he increasingly framed his days as "marking time" until the next trip or workshop rather than building toward anything. When he found himself repeatedly declining invitations to lead new STEM-art initiatives because he felt there was "no point" and started voicing worries that his best years were behind him, his primary care doctor, concerned by this change in outlook at an annual wellness visit, suggested a mental health evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: Lately I just feel like the future doesn’t hold much for me and that the meaningful part of my life is already over.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this low, gray feeling in my chest, like the volume on everything enjoyable has been turned down, and even when I’m painting or at chess club I’m going through the motions without really feeling much of anything about it.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: I get tired so easily now that even a morning of light errands or a couple of hours in my studio leaves me feeling like I’ve hit a wall and need to sit in my chair for the rest of the afternoon, even though I haven’t really done anything strenuous.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: For the past few years I’ve had this steady sense that my life already peaked back when I was running projects at the lab, and no matter how many clubs I join or trips we plan, it all feels like I’m just filling time until the clock runs out rather than moving toward anything that really matters.
